source.title: Predicting the Generalization Gap in Deep Networks with Margin Distributions
source.authors: Yiding Jiang; Dilip Krishnan; H. Mobahi; Samy Bengio

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper and appendices; no material cut-off or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether measured properties of trained networks predict generalization gap, using normalized margin distributions and regression rather than the sharpness measurement specified in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its own margin-distribution predictor and ablations. Cited results about fitting random labels are not this study's results. Its margin measurements do not test the magnitude-aware sharpness named in V7.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a margin-distribution predictor of generalization gaps, which fits none of V1–V8. It does not measure magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, so its predictor comparisons do not test V7. Width, dropout and label corruption vary in the training pool, but the reported results do not isolate the effects specified in V1, V2 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that normalized margin distributions across multiple layers predict generalization gaps well in their tested settings, with quartile summaries combined in log space performing best and hidden-layer information contributing strongly. They propose improved losses and generalization theories as future work, rather than demonstrating improved classifier generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Measures normalized margin distributions and predicts generalization gap by regression; it does not reproduce the claim's sharpness measurement or the original studies' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictive fit varies with normalization, log versus linear transformation, single-layer versus multi-layer features, signature type, architecture and dataset. The paper reports weaker prediction for ResNet CIFAR-10 and notes limited diversity of gaps there.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized multi-layer margin summaries predict generalization gaps: held-out-fold R² is 0.90 for CNNs on CIFAR-10, 0.81 for ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10, and 0.96 for ResNet-32 on CIFAR-100. Ablations assess the predictor's features rather than magnitude-aware sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A linear regression on log-transformed normalized margin-distribution summaries from four layers predicts generalization gaps within the studied CNN and ResNet model pools on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

record.problems: ResNet CIFAR-10 has a narrower reported generalization-gap range; the authors say residuals are less evenly distributed and speculate that the models do not cover the full space of generalization behavior. No uncertainty intervals for the reported R² values are given. One CNN CIFAR-10 adjusted R² differs across prose, table, and figure caption.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The main cohort-level predictor and aggregate comparisons are recorded, along with the reported ablation and single-layer adjusted R² results; held-out-fold k-fold R² is included for the three primary cohorts.

untested.parts: Almost-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels. The study uses 20% corruption, not fully random labels, and does not report the required paired results.
Test-error behavior beyond the width needed for zero training error. Width variation is reported only as part of the predictor's model pool.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, the contribution of local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning, switching optimizers, and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that reduce those effects. All reported training uses batch size 128.

The effect of adding dropout on held-out error, small-data failures, excessive-dropout underfitting, and removing dropout together with weight decay under augmentation. Dropout settings are varied without reporting these contrasts.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps among low-training-loss models, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus an equal number of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T6 applies relative to the eight specified versions. The paper cites the random-label finding and studies a related generalization predictor, but neither tests nor operationally uses a listed effect. All row states are cannot_determine relative to these versions; this does not dispute the reported predictor performance. The predictor pool includes deliberately reduced-capacity models, so it also does not uniformly satisfy V7's similarly low training-loss condition.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether models that fit random labels generalize on natural labels, or whether random-label test accuracy stays at chance.
Varies network width but does not test whether test error keeps falling beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Although dropout appears among varied training settings, the paper does not report whether adding dropout lowers test error in the regimes described by this version.
Measures normalized margin distributions, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or whether that sharpness ranks generalization gaps better than norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples and retrain.

rows.stage_stated: Trained for 380 epochs with SGD with momentum; minibatch size 128
rows.operation_detail: Fit a linear predictor of generalization gap from the full 20-dimensional normalized-margin quartile signature using log transform; report adjusted R².
rows.measure: Adjusted R² for predicting generalization gap
rows.value: 0.94 in Table 1; Figure 2 text reports R̄² of 0.96
rows.note: Aggregate across 216 networks; the paper gives differing adjusted R² values in the prose and Table 1/Figure 2 caption.
rows.check: Own predictor performance, not a claim-effect row. Adjusted R² is 0.94 in Table 1 and the Figure 2 caption; only the Section 4.1 prose says 0.96.
